---
title: "Rules and project instructions"
---

Put stable, human-reviewed project guidance in instruction files. Here, `AGENTS.md` is the common source. `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` adapters import it where supported. Antigravity also needs its verified project-rules mechanism. A file name alone does not guarantee discovery.

Each harness loads and prioritises instructions differently:

- OpenCode traverses project `AGENTS.md` upward and falls back to `CLAUDE.md`.
- Codex layers root-to-current-directory files, with nearer files later.
- Claude layers `CLAUDE.md` files and managed policy.
- Antigravity rules have activation modes. There is no documented automatic `AGENTS.md` import.

Check the installed product's rules page and the context it actually loaded.

Keep instructions to the scope, safe-data boundary, commands, conventions, and verification steps. Separate project rules from personal or global preferences. Ask the agent what it loaded, then verify its answer against the files and documentation.

Rules are not access control. A model may ignore them, another instruction may override them, or a tool may bypass them. Use least-privilege permissions, a disposable environment, and deterministic checks.

::: {.callout-tip}
Before saving repeated knowledge, decide where it belongs: a one-off prompt, project instruction, global instruction, skill, memory or log, or deterministic script. Choose the smallest place that fits.
:::
